First reasoned review, 2026-10-17

Verdicts (SHA-256 prefixes):
36ea1050141c  MALICIOUS  StormAttack service-DLL/Active Setup injector
7333e03ae65c  MALICIOUS  Same StormAttack injector, alternate PE header/layout
147f86fb3903  MALICIOUS  Kawaii-Unicorn multi-payload/infected PE container

Method and limits
-----------------
Ran atomscan and cleave facts separately for all three original paths. Used
Rizin disassembly, pefile section/header inspection, dnfile/dncil IL decoding,
and independent byte reconstruction. Samples were never executed. The three
provided Triage report pages were inaccessible; their scores and collector
filenames were not used as proof. This review does not attribute the bundle
to the long list of families in its filename.

36ea1050141c and 7333e03ae65c
--------------------------
Both contain the same x86 .text implementation. In the overlapping original
file bytes only 254 bytes differ: DOS stub, section raw sizes, and part of the
IAT. The embedded payload begins at 0x5060 in both.

The entry stub calls 0x401cb0. Its mode branches call the following routines:
* 0x402460: FindResourceA/SizeofResource/LoadResource/LockResource -> allocated
  buffer -> 0x4023c0 -> CreateFileA/WriteFile. The installer passes resource
  type DLL and ID 101, constructing a System32/StormServer.dll destination.
* 0x401260: builds an expandable SystemRoot/System32 DLL path, opens
  HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters, deletes
  ServiceDLL, and writes the replacement REG_EXPAND_SZ with RegSetValueExA.
* 0x401150: selects a child image (calc, notepad, IE fallbacks), CreateProcessA,
  VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory of the DLL path, resolves LoadLibraryA
  through GetModuleHandleA/GetProcAddress, and passes the result as the
  CreateRemoteThread entry with the remote path as its argument.
* 0x401900: obtains its module path and a GUID, creates an Active Setup
  Installed Components subkey, writes StubPath, reads/patches its own image
  with CRT I/O, writes a copy, and calls CreateProcessA on that path.
* 0x401390: GetModuleFileNameA -> GetShortPathNameA -> COMSPEC lookup; builds
  /c del <own-short-path> > nul and starts the shell, then resumes/closes it.

The loaded configuration selects mode 3 (Active Setup), with the service/DLL
injection branches also present. Family-specific Storm server/welcome banners
and the embedded STORM command format corroborate StormAttack identity.
The retained four hostile findings cover injection-linked service hijacking,
Active Setup, shell self-deletion, and family identity. No Remcos/WannaCry
behavior was inferred from the filenames.

These are damaged specimens: their embedded DLL has no import directory or
executable section and its entry at RVA 0x741a resolves into zero bytes.
The IAT contains bound/resolved legacy addresses. Thus static attack code is
verified, but successful deployment/injection of these exact copies is not.
The existing descriptions already say code/profile rather than observed
successful execution, and no target-specific exceptions were added.

147f86fb3903
------------
The outer PE identifies itself in resources as Kawaii-Unicorn (UEFI). Its
VB6 entry at 0x4013d4 passes the VB5 header to the runtime. Native form code
around 0x42a0d0 reads the current App.Path/EXEName image into a byte array,
randomizes a byte index/value (rtcRandomize/Rnd and conversion/modulo calls),
stores AL through the array data pointer at 0x42a553, writes a replica through
__vbaPutOwner3, launches it with rtcShell, and has cmd rename/.die cleanup. The
existing polymorphic replication and family detections are supported; byte
mutation is not evidence of encryption or victim-document destruction.
The .data raw pointer is malformed (0xf002c000), and .text is writable without
an executable section flag. These properties do not identify an extra family.

Embedded Action.dll at 0x7501c:
Plugin.Run -> Packet.Read -> LEB128.Read -> command-string switch. Task handlers
include firewall off via hidden cmd /c, Task Manager restrictions via registry
writes, Defender WMI ExclusionPath additions, Run/Userinit and logon tasks,
restore-point enumeration and SRRemoveRestorePoint, and process-critical
controls. BSOD.Run checks administrative membership, calls RtlAdjustPrivilege
with privilege 19, Enable=true, CurrentThread=false, then NtRaiseHardError with
response option 6. This is a deliberately fatal-error operation, not an API
name alone. The Command Prompt handler writes DisableCMD under Policies\Explorer,
so the old blanket claim that both tools are disabled was unwarranted.

Embedded javaws.exe at 0x26eecf:
Its entry at RVA 0x1430c leads to an altered x64 loader, stack-constructs
VirtualAlloc, allocates 0x61be bytes with MEM_COMMIT|MEM_RESERVE and PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE,
copies 0x4615 bytes from RVA 0xfde9, and decodes the first 0x3fe0 bytes backwards.
The key starts at r9d=0x15c13, adds r10d=0x92819200 and rotates left one bit per
byte. Independent decoding recovers the Azov Kasimir mutex, ProgramData and
rdpclient paths plus API tables. The decoded code validates MZ, PE, AMD64 and
PE32+ headers at offsets 0x1ccc..0x1d66 and contains file read/write, traversal,
loader-copy and executable-memory routines. This independently corroborates
the existing Azov encrypted file-infector fingerprint; the Oracle host name
alone establishes neither benignness nor a malicious family. Removed the
unrelated B0024 single-instance mapping from that static loader signature.

Managed ColorGenerator at 0x2e0acf:
MyApplication -> Form21.InitializeComponent -> FHHF06. FHHF00/FHHF02 reconstruct
31744 bytes from a .cctor string: replace X->4, |->-, *->-00, }->0, split, and
Convert.ToByte(base 16). FHHF06 uses Type.InvokeMember(Load, InvokeMethod) on
System.Reflection.Assembly; NASDNNNSN chooses a type and GetMethod(AddContext).
FHHF07 invokes it with resource/key/assembly arguments.

The recovered assembly is a card-game-shaped DLL with an added AOCMS loader.
AOCMS.AddContext waits 25.5 seconds, obtains a resource bitmap from the original
entry assembly, calls III14 to collect R/G/B bytes in column-major order,
XORs with a repeated ASCII key and the final-byte-derived mask, reads a four-byte
length prefix, GZip-decompresses, Assembly.Loads and invokes EntryPoint.
Thus the hidden second assembly really uses RGB steganography; the visible
ColorGenerator pixel/color UI methods do not themselves perform that extraction.

Resource jRcwPZY is a 523x523 RGBA PNG inside serialized Bitmap data. Independent
PNG parsing finds broken IDAT CRCs, malformed later chunk boundaries and a zlib
error. A native PE occurs within that corrupted resource span. No managed
CreateProcess or temporary-directory call exists in the visible IL: those API
strings belong to embedded native data. The old native-temp-dropper finding
asserted an unproven data flow and was removed. The damaged PNG prevented full
recovery of the final managed stage; no final-stage family claim is made.
Other embedded members include a silent SFX with a configured mining batch,
a Petite-packed image, and additional native images. Mining pool/wallet options
alone do not establish unauthorized cryptojacking or executable renaming.

Trait placement and detection changes
------------------------------------
* Namespace/function measurements moved to metadata/binary/{symbols/compiler,
  code/complexity}, with neutral names and notable severity. Signing/version
  data no longer changes the meaning of those measurements.
* RGB/GetObject API co-occurrence moved to micro-behaviors/ui/graphics/image as
  a neutral reference profile. The byte-array profile now requires three getter
  results stored into a byte array, rather than RGB names or a generic CIL call
  sequence. The superseded, otherwise-unused generic component was removed.
* Old bitmap activation composites reference the corrected byte-array profile;
  the two raw bitmap/reflection-only composites now require it too. The visible
  hex wrapper no longer receives five invented bitmap/native-stage conclusions.
* Added substituted-hex executable concealment and assembly-activation coverage
  under anti-static/encoding/custom and execution/payload/module-load.
* Plain TaskMgr/CMD policy/API co-occurrence and ntdll hard-error references
  moved to their neutral registry/syscall homes. Added task-plugin and explicit
  shutdown-privilege/fatal-error coverage in remote-command/tasking and impact.
* Pool/wallet option atoms and their composite moved to process/argument/option;
  the pair is notable and says nothing about renaming or unauthorized mining.
* Updated exact consumers and focused fixture expectations. Parent selectors
  now see the neutral observations; no new directory partition was introduced.
  No dependent-package exception, file hash gate or collector-name gate was used.

Focused checks
--------------
RGB synthetic PE fixtures: API-only negative, getter/array positive, missing
array-store negative. PicoScope profiler/imaging context controls preserved.
Actual decoded AOCMS assembly matches the stronger RGB byte-array profile.
Managed wrapper controls remove encoded MZ or InvokeMember independently.
Plugin controls remove a task verb or change only the fatal response option;
API-name evidence remains present in the latter negative control. Arbitrary
fixture filenames verify that identity is not gated on collection names.
The new activation, tasking and crash rules have precision 7.5, 9.4 and 8.9,
respectively; those scores supplement the execution-path evidence above.
